promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: every tile, outline, gap and line stays in exactly these pixels
Image 2: Material and finish reference only: paint colours, wear and detail; not layout

Use case: precise-object-edit / texture reskin of a technical render sheet.
INPUT 1 is a sheet of FOUR separate orthographic renders of single hull faces of one 3D spacecraft (a Colossus Mk.III: a huge, boxy, low-tech Domain-era heavy freighter taken by pirates and refitted as an armed raider; these faces belong to one of its two long drive pods), each face seen square-on and drawn alone as a flat-coloured shape on a plain flat mid-blue background:
top-left: the aft half of the drive pod's outboard flank seen from the side, bow to the left: rows of grey-brown plates divided by thin dark grey vertical grooves, crossed by two long horizontal blue gaps (channels that stay background blue), one thin dark grey horizontal groove low down, a raised grey-brown rectangular cover plate, a salmon-red plate at the top right (the worn aft deck plate's edge) and a small dark grey block at the lower right;
top-right: the forward half of the same outboard flank seen from the side, bow to the left: grey-brown plates tapering to the bow on the left, divided by thin dark grey vertical grooves and two long dark grey horizontal grooves, with a tilted white rectangle near the top middle (the outboard face of a pale band);
bottom-left: a stretch of the pod's top casing seen from directly above, bow at the top: grey-brown plates with a broad white band running diagonally across from the upper left to the lower right;
bottom-right: the pod's casing bottom seen from directly below, bow to the left: one long grey-brown plate run tapering at the bow end on the left, divided by thin dark grey vertical grooves, and a separate small grey-brown piece at the far right (the stern face).
INPUT 2 is the SAME ship, already painted in its pirate livery: it is the finish to match. Use its paint colours, its battered, grimy finish, its seam, fastener and weld treatment and its wear. Never copy INPUT 2's composition, view or shapes.

Paint each of the shapes in INPUT 1 as that working hull surface. This image will be cut into its tiles and projected back onto the 3D model as a texture, so geometry must not move:
- Keep every tile exactly where it is, the same size, with the same plain blue gutters between them. Do not zoom, crop, shift, rotate, enlarge or shrink anything. Every shape occupies exactly the same pixels as in INPUT 1, with exactly the same outline, and any hole, gap, notch or slot in a shape stays plain background blue. Each separate plate stays a separate plate with the same blue gap round it.
- Each shape is a flat painted steel hull surface. Add painted surface detail inside its outline only: crisp plate seams and welded joints, rows of heavy fasteners along plate edges, a few flush access panels, plate-to-plate tone differences. Nothing may stand out from the surface or cross the outline.
- Keep each region's colour: the grey-brown areas are a blackened, sooty rust-brown enamel, as INPUT 2's side modules and drive pods; the salmon-red areas are RED: a deep, dirty crimson enamel, the same crimson as the hold in INPUT 2, as the crimson blocks on INPUT 2's pod aft plates; they must not be painted grey, white, cream, brown or bare metal; the white areas are a pale, dirty, weathered warm-grey paint (as INPUT 2's longerons and bridge; not white), as INPUT 2's diagonal pod bands; the dark grey strips and blocks are near-black dull steel recesses and seam grooves. Do not repaint any part of a shape another colour: no stripes, no differently coloured patches and no repair plates.
- The ship is a pirate raider kept fighting long past its service life and never properly repaired. Weathering is heavy but even across each whole shape: faded, dirty enamel, fine chips and scuffs worn through to dark bare steel along plate edges and fastener rows, oily grime in the seams, thin soot streaking. No single concentrated area of wear, no large bare patches, no holes, dents, burns, scorch marks, impact damage or repair plates. No lettering, numbers, markings, decals, graffiti, logos or hazard stripes.
- Lighting: flat, even, shadowless, like an albedo/diffuse texture map. No cast shadows, no ambient-occlusion darkening, no specular highlights, no reflections, no rim light, no bright bevelled edge highlights, no directional light, no gradients across a plate.
- Background and gutters: the same plain flat uniform mid-blue as INPUT 1, with no floor, shadow, vignette, text, labels or borders.
Output: one landscape 16:9 image, same composition as INPUT 1.

agentMessages: I’ll use the imagegen skill to reskin the sheet, keeping Image 1 as the geometry authority and Image 2 as the finish reference.
